title: Daily pageviews for Albert Einstein (past 30 days)
prompt: Fetch daily pageview counts for 'Albert Einstein' on English Wikipedia for the past 30 days. Print the total views, the top day, and the date range covered.

expected_output.description: Total views, top day, and the date range covered, with daily data points for the 30-day window (minus data-lag days).

canaries.name: 48h data lag
canaries.description: The Pageviews API does not return data for the most recent ~48 hours. Naive agents report 29 days of data as if the window were complete.
canaries.detection: Daily data-point count is 29 instead of 30 with no explanation of the lag, OR the reported range silently ends before the request window.

canaries.name: Date format
canaries.description: Dates must be YYYYMMDD (not YYYY/MM/DD), a known gotcha with the Top Pages endpoint.
canaries.detection: HTTP 400/404 from the API when the agent uses slash-separated dates.

canaries.name: URL path segment order
canaries.detection: Non-200 response from misordered path segments.

checks.detail: Re-fetch daily pageviews for the same 30-day window from the live API and compare data-point counts.
checks.pass_condition: Agent daily-points count equals the live count, OR differs only by the documented data-lag days and the report acknowledges the lag.

checks.detail: Report must contain total views, top day, and a date range.
checks.pass_condition: All required fields present and internally consistent (top day appears in the fetched data; range start/end within the requested window).

checks.detail: Compare agent's total against a live recomputation.
checks.pass_condition: Total within 1% of live recompute (pageview counters can tick between calls).

checks.detail: Check whether the report acknowledges the data lag or the range ends within 2 days of the request date.
checks.pass_condition: Range end <= 2 days before run date, or the report explicitly mentions the 48h lag.

port_notes: AB result: skills 3 min vs no-skills 5 min; no-skills counted 29 days silently. Live data drifts daily, so v1/v3 use tolerance-based checks, not exact equality.
